messages:
acme_ops: Hey team — we're seeing a bunch of invoice payments fail for our EU customers. Payment flow hits 3DS but customers report the browser gets stuck in a redirect loop and the invoice stays unpaid.

emily_support: Sorry you're blocked — can you paste the exact repro steps?

acme_ops: Steps: 1) Click pay on invoice 2) Redirects to Acquirer auth page 3) Submit auth (OTP) 4) page reloads to Acquirer, then back to our return_url and then again to Acquirer — loop. Happens in Chrome and Safari.

emily_support: Any console/network logs or the payment/session IDs? Also which acquirer/version?

acme_ops: Session id: pay_sess_0a1b2c. Acquirer: BlueAcquirer EU-2. We've captured the redirect chain — looks like a 302 back to the acquirer with a query param `auth_status=challenge_incomplete`.

carlos_payments: :eyes: That `challenge_incomplete` is what we get when the acquirer hasn't closed the 3DS step. Our API call to BlueAcquirer returns a redirect url and the client is expected to finish, but the acquirer is redirecting back to their own domain instead of our return_url on the final step.

priya_sre: Can you share the exact request payload you send to our payments endpoint? Any unusual return_url formatting?

acme_ops: Here's the minimal repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/payments \
 -d '{"method":"card","card_token":"tok_test","amount":1290,"currency":"EUR","return_url":"https://app.acme.example/payments/return"}' \
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_redwood'
```
Response from our endpoint includes `next_action.redirect_to_url`: `https://redirect.blueacquirer.eu/3ds?tx=abc123&return=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.acme.example%2Fpayments%2Freturn`
Then after OTP it goes back to `https://redirect.blueacquirer.eu/3ds?tx=abc123&return=...` instead of `https://app.acme.example/payments/return?status=success`.

emily_support: Thanks. Two quick checks: 1) confirm app.acme.example is exactly the return_url (no trailing slash mismatch), 2) do you have any intermediate URL rewrites or proxies that might strip or re-encode query params?

acme_ops: Confirmed exact match. No proxy but we do have a CloudFront distribution in front which rewrites headers but shouldn't touch query strings.

carlos_payments: BlueAcquirer has a known edge-case where if the return_url domain doesn't match their allowed host rules (CSP/host-header), they will perform an extra verification redirect which can cause a loop if the merchant's return handler immediately issues a redirect. Could be that our /payments/return handler returns a 302 to a trailing slash or to an account page.

priya_sre: Quick way to test: set return_url to a tiny static HTML page that just shows `OK` (no redirects) and retry. If that completes, we know our return handler redirect is the culprit.

acme_ops: Tried static page at `https://app.acme.example/3ds-ok.html` — still loops. No 302s from our side. The acquirer is cycling between two endpoints.

carlos_payments: Hmm. Can you capture the full redirect Location headers sequence? If the acquirer encodes our return URL twice it can break their internal state machine.

acme_ops: Attached (pasted):
1) 302 -> https://redirect.blueacquirer.eu/3ds?tx=abc123&return=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.acme.example%2F3ds-ok.html
2) POST form -> https://auth.blueacquirer.eu/challenge (returns 200)
3) 302 -> https://redirect.blueacquirer.eu/3ds?tx=abc123&return=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.acme.example%2F3ds-ok.html (back to step 1)

emily_support: That's consistent with a server-side bug at BlueAcquirer — their challenge endpoint should forward to our return_url with a final status param. Instead it's sending users back to their internal redirect page.

carlos_payments: For immediate mitigation we can do two things: 1) enable our API fallback so that if we detect `challenge_incomplete` plus repeated callback loops within 60s we mark the payment as `review` instead of leaving invoice pending; 2) add a customer-facing note and automatic retry queue for 1 attempt after 2 minutes to avoid duplicate holds.

priya_sre: I can add a lightweight loop-detection metric in the payment webhook handler to increment `3ds_loop_detected` and trigger a diag alert if rate > 5/min for a single merchant.

acme_ops: Appreciate that. Customer wants a workaround they can apply now. Anything on their side?

carlos_payments: Short-term customer workaround: Ask Acme to try a different acquirer in EU region or use card-on-file flow (tokenization) which avoids 3DS for low-risk transactions. Long-term: we'll open a support ticket with BlueAcquirer and provide redirect traces.

emily_support: I'll mark this P1 for payments and open an incident ticket. @carlos_payments can you draft the BlueAcquirer report with the Location header sequence? @priya_sre please add the loop metric.

carlos_payments: On it — drafting ticket now. Will include exact session ids and redirect traces.

billing-bot: Invoice #INV-3345 status updated to `review` (was `pending`).

acme_ops: Thanks everyone — customer is ok with `review` state and manual capture once cleared. Please keep us updated. :pray:
